transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sara (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Dana (FinEdge CTO), Samir (Platform Eng), Priya (SRE)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Follow-up on this week's incident where several inference requests hit 5xxs/timeouts during peak load. Discussed root-cause hypotheses (rate-limit thresholds, upstream retries, kv cache invalidation), short-term mitigations, and next steps for a focused benchmark and config changes (timeouts/retries/backoff).

Transcript:
[00:00] Sara (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on — I know last week was rough, so want to go through the incident timeline and next steps. Marco's here to cover the config changes and suggested retries.
[00:16] Dana (FinEdge): thanks Sara. yeah, we had a spike friday afternoon, ~14:20 local. lots of 5xx across our test traffic and a handful of timeouts from the app.
[00:24] Samir: to add, our pods started to see queue buildup — cpu was fine but nvme i/o spiked i think, plus we saw a lot of 429-ish semantics early on, then cascaded into 5xx from the Redwood endpoint.
[00:40] Marco (Redwood-SE): ok, good context. from our side we saw increased tail latency hitting the serving runtime, and some requests were getting retried by your client which amplified load — classic retry storm pattern.
[00:55] Priya (SRE): yes, we do have a simple exponential backoff but it's aggressive (3 retries, short base delay) — we thought retries would help but they may have worsened things.
[01:10] Sara: quick clarifying q: were most of the errors 502/504 or were you seeing 500?
[01:15] Samir: mostly 504s and a bunch of gateway timeouts, a few 500s. the 504s match the timeout window we had configured to the Redwood hosted endpoint.
[01:28] Marco: that suggests requests were hitting the 60s cutoff, or there was a transient saturation on the model worker. we did have a couple of lower-capacity workers in your pilot's dedicated pool at the time due to autoscaler cooldowns.
[01:43] Dana: the autoscaler had a cooldown of 10 minutes which might've prevented quick spin-ups — we were underprovisioned at peak.
[01:50] Marco: right — two things to consider: client-side retry/backoff tuning, and serving-side timeout adjustments and throttling. also we can enable per-customer rate shaping on the router to smooth bursts.
[02:05] Samir: can you expand on rate shaping? is that part of Redwood Dedi or the hosted router?
[02:12] Marco: it's in the routing layer — we can apply token-bucket style rate limits and also burst tokens for short spikes. for your pilot we'd suggest a soft cap at 80% of expected sustained qps and a higher burst for sudden spikes.
[02:29] Priya: i want to be sure we won't see caching invalidation issues — we use prefix caching for common prompts, but when the cache misses we saw heavier load. any suggestions there?
[02:40] Marco: yes, kv cache behavior matters. we'll recommend increasing the cache TTL for your top prefixes and enabling adaptive prefetching; also ensure your clients reuse connections to the SDK to avoid repeated cold starts.
[02:55] Dana: about monitoring — our alerts only caught error-rate but not queue-length; any quick wins?
[03:03] Sara: we can push a dashboard tile for per-route queue depth and 95/99 lat percentiles; Marco can share the Grafana link after the call.
[03:12] Marco: i'll share a dashboard and a small runbook: when 95th > X ms and error-rate > Y then scale up or enable fallback.
[03:22] Dana: fallback is important — we want graceful degradation not hard failures. can Redwood route to a lower-capacity cheaper variant under pressure?
[03:31] Marco: yes — smart routing can failover to a small quantized variant (we called it redwood-lite internally) with slightly different quality but faster tails; you can configure automatic fallback policies.
[03:45] Samir: our legal team also asked about data retention and logs for the incident — do you provide full request traces?
[03:52] Sara: we keep per-request logs in the console; for Private/VPC customers we can provide longer retention and raw traces via S3 delivery, subject to the contract. for hosted we'll share the redacted logs and the audit trail.
[04:05] Priya: security-wise, we need proof of SOC2 and details on KMS integration for keys. this was already requested in the security questionnaire.
[04:14] Sara: got it, i'll resend the SOC 2 report and KMS docs — Marco will include details about encryption-at-rest for cached items too.
[04:23] Marco: on the technical mitigation, here's a concrete plan: reduce client retries to 1 with a higher base delay, set client timeout to 70% of server-side timeout, enable router rate-shaping with token bucket, and increase dedicated pool min nodes during your business hours to avoid autoscaler cooldown gaps.
[04:40] Dana: sounds good. any potential tradeoffs?
[04:44] Marco: tradeoff is potentially higher p99 if we reduce retries (you'll see more immediate errors if the backend is slow), but overall system load will be much smoother and you avoid retry amplification. the fallback to quantized variant will reduce quality a bit; we can measure that with an eval set.
[04:59] Samir: can you share recommended timeout and retry numbers? we want something concrete to put in our config.
[05:06] Marco: recommended: server-side request timeout 60s, client RPC timeout 40s, retries = 1, backoff base = 300ms and multiplier 2, jitter enabled. token-bucket rate limit at 120rps per route with burst 200 for 30s. we'll send the helm snippet.
[05:27] Priya: earlier you mentioned KV cache TTLs — what values?
[05:31] Marco: for your workload i'd start with 30m TTL for popular prefixes, adaptive prefetching on, and ensure cache nodes have enough memory to keep hot keys.
[05:40] Dana: how would we validate quality after enabling quantized fallback — do you have eval tooling?
[05:44] Marco: yes we do — Redwood Optimize has a small eval harness; we can run your prompt set against both the primary and fallback and give a delta report.
[05:55] Sara: ok let's align on immediate actions: Marco will send config, Samir will share logs, Sara will send SOC2 + incident timeline and pricing addendum, then we schedule a benchmark.
[06:05] Dana: quick note — we also saw increased cost because of repeated retries, want to understand bill impact.
[06:11] Sara: we'll include a rough cost delta in the addendum, and Marco will show how batching and cache adjustments can reduce token cost.
[06:20] Samir: timeline question — how fast can you get the helm/rc config?
[06:23] Marco: i can share within 48 hours. the helm snippet for retry/timeouts and router rules is straightforward.
[06:29] Priya: any chance we can run a synthetic spike test with you guys to prove the config?
[06:34] Marco: absolutely — we can coordinate a bench run during low-traffic hours. we recommend a three-phase test: baseline, simulated spike, and ramp-down to measure p50/p95/p99 and 5xx counts.
[06:47] Dana: perfect. also curious about alerting thresholds — what's reasonable for 5xx?
[06:51] Marco: suggest alert if 5xx > 1% sustained for 5 minutes or if p99 latency increases by > 2x from baseline. we'll provide default thresholds.
[07:02] Samir: on the K8s side, we saw a lot of evictions during the window due to node pressure — would dedicated capacity remove that variable?
[07:10] Marco: yes Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk; your dedicated pool is isolated but autoscaler behavior still matters. if you want hard guarantees, Reserved capacity with minimum nodes prevents scale-to-zero during spikes.
[07:23] Priya: how would retries interact with your router rate limits — if we get 429s from router, do you expose Retry-After?
[07:29] Marco: yes we send a Retry-After header; best practice is to honor it and back off. we'll show example client-side snippet to parse it.
[07:38] Dana: last incident detail — some users reported partial responses (truncated) before a 504 — is that on the client or server?
[07:45] Marco: likely server cutoff; if server hits the timeout while streaming it may close the connection. we can increase the server streaming timeout for your route to reduce truncation.
[07:55] Sara: ok, i want to call out a small gotcha we saw: your app uses short-lived ephemeral API keys causing extra auth overhead — if you can rotate less often or reuse tokens per session it reduces auth latency.
[08:07] Dana: noted, we'll review token lifetime.
[08:11] Marco: i'll also attach a small test harness that does connection reuse and shows difference in cold-starts vs warm sessions.
[08:20] Samir: are there any configuration limits on rate-shaping per tenant? we have multiple routes and want per-route caps.
[08:26] Marco: it's per-route and per-tenant; you can configure different caps per route. we'll include examples.
[08:33] Dana: ok great — let's recap next steps.
[08:36] Sara: recap: Marco send helm snippet, retry/timeout guidelines, caching recommendations, dashboard link. Samir upload logs and k8s dump. Sara send SOC2 and incident timeline plus rough cost impact. then schedule benchmark for 2026-03-31.
[08:53] Priya: thanks, please include estimated MTTI (mean time to incident detection) improvements if possible.
[08:58] Marco: will do, i'll note the observability changes and expected detection improvements.
[09:03] Dana: one final question — is there any quick patch to prevent retry storms right now?
[09:08] Marco: yes set client retries to 0 or 1, add jitter, and temporarily lower client concurrency during the spike window. we can push router soft caps to smooth right away.
[09:20] Sara: awesome. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with artifacts.
[09:24] Dana: thanks all. bye.

End of transcript.
